newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia central bank sees 1-2 pct '97 GDP growth. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russia central bank sees 1-2 pct '97 GDP growth. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]

text.p: Russia's Central Bank expects gross domestic product to grow by one-two percent and monthly inflation to average 0.93 (corrects from "1.7 to 1.9") percent in 1997, it said.

Tax as a proportion of GDP will rise to 14 percent from nine percent in 1996 due to government control over tax collection and a cut in state subsidies, the Central Bank said in its 1997 monetary programme, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.

The programme, drafted late last year and currently being discussed by the State Duma lower house of parliament, will be the basis for the 1997 economic programme which Russia is due to sign with the International Monetary Fund.
The IMF has repeatedly delayed monthly payments from its $10 billion loan to Russia because of unsatisfactory tax revenues.

The Central Bank programme forecasts a budget deficit of 3.5 percent of GDP, to be financed in equal proportions by domestic and internal borrowing. The recently approved 1997 budget provides for a 3.85 percent deficit, the same as in 1996.
The fall in the budget deficit will allow the Central Bank to increase money supply at rates higher than inflation, or 1.7-2.2 percent a month, it said.
It said the authorities will try to continue cutting yields on government securities and make changes in yields more smooth.
It also forecast rouble depreciation against the dollar of 8.6 percent annual.
The Central Bank has set a sloping corridor, or band, for the rouble/dollar rate, according to which the rouble will be trading at 5,750-6,350 per dollar on December 31 this year.

The Duma's budget committee recommended the Central Bank to cut interest rates and Treasury bills yields and asked the government to cut budget deficit and the state debt, the committee said in a draft statement approving the programme.
